     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision 975feb3, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98 and 3920258.
     9	The later revisions changed prose, titles, the literature review, layout and
    10	figures, added a zero-covariance remark after `H:homog` and qualified a strict
    11	comparison in `T:first` (not cited here) as asserted only for nonzero
    12	covariance. Every cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at
    13	3920258 and 975feb3. Between these two revisions every cited lemma,
    14	proposition, theorem and equation has the same statement and proof up to
    15	whitespace and braces, with one exception: the statement of `T:full-upper`
    16	(cited only as not formalized) now ends with a cross-reference to Theorem
    17	`T:intro-upper` instead of Goal `G:upper`, and its mathematics is unchanged.
    18	The cited sections `S:model` (the zero-covariance remark and a roadmap

4414	## WaveGreen (whole result)
  4415	
  4416	Defines the wave Green measures `G_s` of the main file
  4417	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `975feb3`) and states
  4418	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lemma, lines 766-792; proof, lines 793-846)
  4419	with nothing supplied. Sources of the measures at `975feb3`: `d = 1`,
  4420	`G(s,y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s}` (proof of `L:white-test`, line 709; again at
  4421	lines 4055 and 7569); `d = 2, 3`, the proof of `L:higher-riesz` (lines
  4422	5106-5114), which quotes Chen (2.5), p. 7:
  4423	`G_h^(2)(dy) = 1_{|y|<h} dy / (2 pi sqrt(h^2 - |y|^2))` and
  4424	`G_h^(3)(dy) = sigma_h(dy)/(4 pi h)`, `sigma_h` the surface measure of the
  4425	radius-`h` sphere, and states "Both have mass `h` and satisfy
  4426	`G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)`" (lines 5113-5114). The list of notation
  4427	(`notes/index/list-of-notation.tex`, line 102) describes `G_t` as the "Wave
  4428	Green measure, with mass `t` and support in the closed radius-`t` ball". The
  4429	mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` is the step of the proof of
  4430	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` at line 825, which `DampedNormsHomog` took as
  4431	the supplied input `GreenMass G`.
  4432	
  4433	Definition. `waveGreen d s` is, for `d = 1`, `(1/2)` Lebesgue measure
  4434	restricted to the open ball `|x| < s`; for `d = 2`, Lebesgue measure with
  4435	density `1_{|x|<s} (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - |x|^2))^(-1)` (inside the ball the root
  4436	is of a positive number, so no `sqrt` or division junk value enters); for
  4437	`d = 3`, `(s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) volume.toSphere`; for every other `d`,
  4438	the zero measure. For `d = 3` this is a DEFINITIONAL CHOICE (Le's decision 4
  4439	for wave L6): Mathlib's `Measure.toSphere` (which satisfies

   100	/-- The wave Green measure `G_s` on `ℝ^d` (main TeX lines 709, 5109-5113;
   101	Chen (2.5)): `d = 1`: `½ 1_{|x|<s} dx`; `d = 2`:
   102	`1_{|x|<s} dx / (2π√(s²-|x|²))`; `d = 3`: `σ_s/(4πs)`, written as
   103	`(s/(4π)) · map (ω ↦ sω) volume.toSphere`, which takes Mathlib's
   104	`Measure.toSphere` as the surface measure of the unit sphere (a definitional
   105	choice, Le's decision 4; see the module doc); other `d`: `0`. -/
   106	def waveGreen : (d : ℕ) → ℝ → Measure (Rd d)
   107	  | 1, s => ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2) • volume.restrict (ball 0 s)
   108	  | 2, s => volume.withDensity ((ball (0 : Rd 2) s).indicator
   109	      fun x => ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * π * Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹))
   110	  | 3, s => ENNReal.ofReal (s / (4 * π)) •
   111	      (volume.toSphere.map fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => s • (ω : Rd 3))
   112	  | _, _ => 0
   113	
   114	/-- Outside `d ∈ {1,2,3}` the definition is the zero measure (a convention;
   115	the manuscript has `d ∈ {1,2,3}`). -/
   116	theorem waveGreen_other (d : ℕ) (h1 : d ≠ 1) (h2 : d ≠ 2) (h3 : d ≠ 3) (s : ℝ) :
   117	    waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   118	  unfold waveGreen; split <;> simp_all

  2637	## QuotientObstruction (whole result)
  2638	
  2639	Formalizes `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` (A physical mask need not preserve
  2640	noise-null tests) of `S:masked-covariance`
  2641	(`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `975feb3`, statement lines
  2642	257-263, proof lines 265-292) in full, with nothing supplied. The wrapper
  2643	`masked_quotient_obstruction_paper` takes exactly the manuscript's
  2644	hypotheses: `d = 2`, `alpha = 1`, `0 < a < 1` (the section's `a = alpha0`),
  2645	`Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`Gamma0`) and the section's `T > 0`. It
  2646	concludes that `Gamma0` with `mu0 = (2 pi)^(-1) dxi_1 delta_0(dxi_2)`
  2647	satisfies `H:homog` (`HomogCovariance 2 1 a Gamma0 mu0`, lines 266-270),
  2648	that `Gamma0 != 0` (the section's standing assumption, lines 5-6, holds for
  2649	this `Gamma`), and that some real `C^infinity` compactly supported mask
  2650	`zeta` on `R^2` admits no real `C` with
  2651	`covW a Gamma0 (zeta F) <= C covW a Gamma0 F` for every test `F` with
  2652	`IsTest T F`. `masked_quotient_obstruction` states the proof's computation
  2653	with the explicit witnesses `zeta = chi(x_1) chi(x_2)`,
  2654	`g = chi(x_1) chi''(x_2)` (`gtest`) and a bump `tau` supported in `(0,T)`
  2655	(the proof chooses `tau` nonnegative and nonzero; the exported existential
  2656	records `IsTest (tau g)`, temporal integrability and positive `timeQ`, not
  2657	these properties of `tau` separately): the test `F = tau g`, the integrability of every
  2658	integrand it evaluates, `V(g) = 0`, `V(zeta g) = J_chi I_chi^2`,
  2659	`covW(F) = 0` and `covW(zeta F) = norm(tau)_a^2 J_chi I_chi^2 > 0`.
  2660	
  2661	Definitional boundary (D1). The noise `W` is not constructed. `E W(F)^2` is
  2662	read as the covariance functional of `E:cov`
  2663	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `975feb3`, lines
  2664	184-187): `covW a Gamma F = int_t int_s |t-s|^(-a) int Gamma(dz) int F(t,x)
  2665	F(s,x-z) dx`, iterated Lean Bochner integrals with time over `R` (equal to
  2666	`[0,T]^2` for the tests used). Because a Bochner integral of a
  2667	non-integrable function is `0`, the values `0` and `> 0` of the witnesses
  2668	come with integrability conclusions (time integrand on `R x R`, spatial
  2669	integrands for every `z` and against `Gamma0`), so they are genuine.
  2670	
  2671	Abstractions. "Compact smooth test `F`" (line 262) is `IsTest T F`:
  2672	`(t,x) -> F t x` is `C^infinity` with compact support and vanishes unless
  2673	`t in (0,T)`. This restricts the tests, so the nonexistence of `C` is
  2674	stronger than over all compact smooth tests. `C` ranges over all reals.
  2675	`Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` is `lineMeasure e2`, the pushforward of
  2676	Lebesgue measure under `t -> t e_2`; the plane `R^2` is
  2677	`EuclideanSpace R (Fin 2)` with coordinates through the volume-preserving
  2678	`plane : R x R -> R^2`. `chi` is Mathlib's `ContDiffBump` with radii `1` and
  2679	`2` (equal to `1` on `[-1,1]`, `0` outside `(-2,2)`); the TeX's explicit
  2680	formula (lines 276-279) is introduced "for example", and evenness of `chi`
  2681	and `J_chi >= 2` are not used.
  2682	
  2683	Proof-route differences. `V(g)` (lines 272-274) is identified with the
  2684	spatial covariance (lines 270-271, "by ordinary Fubini") for every real
  2685	continuous compactly supported `g` through the substitution `x = y + t e_2`
  2686	and Fubini on `R x R^2` (`autocorr_e2`, auxiliary, under a product decay
  2687	bound `PlaneDecay`). Positive definiteness of `Gamma` (line 268) is proved
  2688	directly, `int Gamma(dz) (phi * phi~)(z) = int |int phi(u,v) dv|^2 du`, not
  2689	through the spectral measure. The spectral identity (lines 266-267, "Fourier
  2690	inversion on Schwartz tests") is proved by one-dimensional Fourier inversion
  2691	(`Integrable.fourierInv_fourier_eq`) for the marginal
  2692	`Phi(u) = int phi(u,v) dv`, whose Fourier transform is the restriction of the
  2693	two-dimensional Fourier transform of `phi` to the first axis; the Schwartz
  2694	decay of that restriction gives the integrability inversion needs. The
  2695	remaining fields of `H:homog` (Radon, even, tempered with `k = 2`, scaling
  2696	`Gamma(cA) = c Gamma(A)` for every set `A`) come from the line-measure
  2697	lemmas. Positivity of `norm(tau)_a^2` (lines 287-289) uses
  2698	`TimeSchur.time_schur_paper` for integrability and a product of two
  2699	intervals on which the integrand is positive.
  2700	
  2701	Hypotheses carried but unused: none of the wrapper's (`0 < a` is used by
  2702	`TimeSchur.time_schur_paper` and by `HomogCovariance`). The general lemmas
  2703	state their own hypotheses: `isEven_lineMeasure` holds for every `v`, the
  2704	other line-measure lemmas need `norm(v) = 1`; `covW_tensor` needs no
  2705	integrability.
  2706	
  2707	Not formalized: the noise `W` and its test-noise completion (D1); the claim
  2708	"This is not spatial white noise in dimension two" (line 270) is not a
  2709	theorem of the module (the refutation `refutations/quotient-obstruction/WhiteNoise.lean`
  2710	shows `Gamma0 != volume`).

  2713	the proof route and have no rows of their own.

    78	/-- Auxiliary: the point `(u, v)` of `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`. -/

    87	/-- Auxiliary: `plane` is volume preserving from `ℝ × ℝ` to `ℝ²`. -/

    91	    (volume_preserving_finTwoArrow ℝ).symm
    92	  convert h using 1
    93	  funext p
    94	  ext i; fin_cases i <;> rfl

    98	  have h : plane = (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ∘
    99	      (MeasurableEquiv.finTwoArrow (α := ℝ)).symm := by
   100	    funext p; rfl
   101	  rw [h]
   102	  exact (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin 2 → ℝ)).measurableEmbedding.comp
   103	    (MeasurableEquiv.finTwoArrow (α := ℝ)).symm.measurableEmbedding

   585	
   586	/-- The noise covariance functional of `E:cov` (main TeX file
   587	`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`, 975feb3, lines 184-187) read as
   588	`E W(F)² = ∫∫ |t-s|^{-a} ∫ Γ(dz) ∫ F(t,x) F(s,x-z) dx dt ds` for a real test `F`
   589	(a definitional D1 reading; `W` itself is not constructed).  Time integrals run over
   590	`ℝ`; for tests supported in `(0,T)` this is the integral over `[0,T]²`.  An
   591	iterated Bochner integral: it is the manuscript's quantity where the integrands are
   592	integrable, which the theorems below prove for the tests they use. -/
   593	def covW {d : ℕ} (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (F : ℝ → Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   594	  ∫ t, ∫ s, |t - s| ^ (-a) * ∫ z, (∫ x, F t x * F s (x - z)) ∂Γ
   595	
   596	/-- The spatial covariance `∫ Γ(dz) ∫ f(x) g(x-z) dx` (the spatial factor of
   597	`covW`). -/
   598	def spatialCov {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (f g : Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   599	  ∫ z, (∫ x, f x * g (x - z)) ∂Γ
   600	
   601	/-- The temporal factor `‖τ‖_a² = ∫∫ τ(t) τ(s) |t-s|^{-a} dt ds`. -/
   602	def timeQ (a : ℝ) (τ : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   603	  ∫ t, ∫ s, τ t * τ s * |t - s| ^ (-a)
   604	
   605	/-- The manuscript's `V(g) = ∫_ℝ (∫_ℝ g(x₁, x₂) dx₂)² dx₁` (TeX lines 272-274). -/
   606	def margV (g : Rd 2 → ℝ) : ℝ := ∫ u, (∫ v, g (plane (u, v))) ^ 2

   609	`‖τ‖_a² · ∫ Γ(dz) ∫ g(x) g(x-z) dx` (TeX lines 286-290).  No integrability is
   610	needed: constants are pulled out of Bochner integrals. -/
   611	theorem covW_tensor {d : ℕ} (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (τ : ℝ → ℝ) (g : Rd d → ℝ) :

   613	  unfold covW timeQ spatialCov
   614	  have h : ∀ t s : ℝ, ∫ z, (∫ x, τ t * g x * (τ s * g (x - z))) ∂Γ =
   615	      τ t * τ s * ∫ z, (∫ x, g x * g (x - z)) ∂Γ := by
   616	    intro t s
   617	    rw [← integral_const_mul]
   618	    refine integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun z => ?_)
   619	    dsimp only
   620	    rw [← integral_const_mul]
   621	    refine integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
   622	    dsimp only
   623	    ring

   626	  refine integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun t => ?_)
   627	  dsimp only
   628	  rw [← integral_mul_const]
   629	  refine integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun s => ?_)

   633	/-- Auxiliary: continuous compactly supported functions have product decay. -/
   634	theorem planeDecay_of_hasCompactSupport {g : Rd 2 → ℝ} (hc : Continuous g)
   635	    (hs : HasCompactSupport g) : PlaneDecay g := by
   636	  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hc.bounded_above_of_compact_support hs
   637	  obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := hs.isCompact.isBounded.subset_closedBall 0
   638	  set R' := max R 0
   639	  have hM0 : 0 ≤ M := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hM 0)
   640	  refine ⟨M * (1 + R') ^ 4, by positivity, fun p => ?_⟩
   641	  by_cases hp : g (plane p) = 0
   642	  · rw [hp, norm_zero]
   643	    have := wt_pos p.1; have := wt_pos p.2
   644	    positivity
   645	  have hn : ‖plane p‖ ≤ R' := by
   646	    have := hR (subset_tsupport g hp)
   647	    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] at this
   648	    exact this.trans (le_max_left _ _)
   649	  have hw : ∀ r : ℝ, |r| ≤ R' → ((1 + R') ^ 2)⁻¹ ≤ wt r := by
   650	    intro r hr

     1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
    86	\end{equation}
    87	
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}
    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}
    99	  For a real $H$, the same assertion holds after complexification.
   100	\end{proposition}
   101	
   102	\begin{proof}
   103	  Schwartz decay of $k_R$ and polynomial growth of $\mu$ show that
   104	  $\rho_R(\eta)$ is finite at every $\eta$. On compact sets of $\eta$, the
   105	  integrands have a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence therefore
   106	  makes $\rho_R$ continuous, and $\nu_R$ is Radon. Since $\zeta$ is real,
   107	  $k_R(-u) = \overline{k_R(u)}$. Evenness of $\mu$ gives evenness of $\rho_R$.
   108	  Tonelli's theorem gives
   109	  \[
   110	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(u)|\mu(B(y+u,r))\ud u.
   111	  \]
   112	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth} and $\|k_R\|_1 = L$ give
   113	  \eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}. Polynomial growth on centered balls proves
   114	  temperedness by the same dyadic argument as above.
   115	
   116	  Bochner Fourier integration gives
   117	  \[
   118	    \widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)
   119	    = c_d\int k_R(\xi-\eta)\widehat{F}(\eta)\ud\eta.
   120	  \]
   121	  For scalar Schwartz functions this follows by Fourier inversion and absolute
   122	  integrability. It follows next for finite-rank Hilbert-valued functions. For
   123	  general $F$, take projections onto the successive spans of a countable
   124	  orthonormal basis of its separable range closure. They converge pointwise in
   125	  norm. The Schwartz bounds on $F$ dominate the Fourier integrals, proving the
   126	  identity by dominated convergence. In a finite-dimensional space the full
   127	  identity projection suffices; the zero space is immediate. The triangle
   128	  inequality and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yield
   129	  \[
   130	    \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2
   131	    \le c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   132	  \]
   133	  Integrating against $\mu$ and applying Tonelli's theorem proves
   134	  \eqref{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}. Its right side is finite by Schwartz decay
   135	  and temperedness of $\nu_R$. This proves
   136	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}.
   137	\end{proof}

   139	\subsection{Temporal completion and the original noise}
   140	
   141	\begin{lemma}[Temporal covariance completion]\label{L:masked-time-completion}
   142	  Let $T > 0$. The form
   143	  \[
   144	    \langle f,g\rangle_a
   145	    = \int_0^T\int_0^T f(t)g(s)|t-s|^{-a}\ud t\ud s
   146	  \]
   147	  is positive semidefinite on real compact smooth tests. Its null-quotient
   148	  completion $H_a$ is separable. The inclusion of tests extends continuously
   149	  from $L^2(0,T)$, with
   150	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-time-schur}
   151	    \|f\|_a^2 \le \frac{2T^{1-a}}{1-a}\|f\|_2^2.
   152	  \end{equation}
   153	  In its complexification the norm is given by the same double integral with
   154	  $f(t)\overline{f(s)}$. In particular, bounded measurable amplitudes on a
   155	  subinterval, extended by zero, belong to this completion.
   156	\end{lemma}
   157	
   158	\begin{proof}
   159	  Write $\Gamma_E$ for Euler's Gamma function. Away from the null diagonal,
   160	  \[
   161	    |t-s|^{-a} = \frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}\int_0^\infty
   162	    \lambda^{a-1}e^{-\lambda|t-s|}\ud\lambda.
   163	  \]
   164	  This follows by substitution in the defining Gamma integral. Moreover,
   165	  \[
   166	    e^{-\lambda|t-s|}
   167	    = \int_{-\infty}^{\min(t,s)}2\lambda
   168	    e^{-\lambda(t-u)}e^{-\lambda(s-u)}\ud u.
   169	  \]
   170	  For each $\lambda > 0$ its quadratic form is an integral of a square. All
   171	  exchanges for compact smooth tests are absolutely integrable because the
   172	  kernel row integral is at most $2T^{1-a}/(1-a)$. The same bound and $2|xy| \le
   173	  |x|^2+|y|^2$ prove~\eqref{E:masked-time-schur}. A countable $L^2$-dense family
   174	  of compact smooth tests is consequently dense in $H_a$, proving separability.
   175	  The complex quadratic form is the sum of those of the real and imaginary
   176	  parts, since symmetry cancels the imaginary cross term. Thus, the same bound
   177	  holds after complexification. Smooth density in $L^2$, together with the Schur
   178	  bound on the absolute bilinear form, extends the inclusion and the integral
   179	  identity to $L^2$. This includes the stated interval amplitudes. This proves
   180	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   181	\end{proof}
   182	
   183	Let $\mathcal{D}$ consist of finite sums $F(t,x) = \sum_j\tau_j(t)f_j(x)$ with
   184	real $\tau_j \in C_c^\infty(0,T)$ and real Schwartz $f_j$. These give
   185	$H_a$-valued Schwartz functions of $x$. Let $W$ denote the original real
   186	isonormal noise in~\eqref{E:cov}.
   187	
   188	\begin{proposition}[Completion on the same noise]\label{P:masked-noise-completion}
   189	  The space $\mathcal{D}$ belongs to the original test-noise completion and
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}
   191	    \E W(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   192	    \|\widehat{F}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  Define the auxiliary seminorm
   195	  \[
   196	    N_R(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   197	    \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
   198	  \]
   199	  Then $F \mapsto W(\zeta_RF)$ extends as a contraction from the null-quotient
   200	  completion for $N_R$ into the original $L^2(\Omega)$. The extension is
   201	  centered and jointly Gaussian. For finitely many real $F_1,\ldots,F_m \in
   202	  \mathcal{D}$, their masked covariance matrix is bounded in positive
   203	  semidefinite order by the matrix of auxiliary inner products. This gives
   204	  covariance comparison for every finite linear Gaussian image and every convex
   205	  norm power $p \ge 1$.
   206	\end{proposition}
   207	
   208	\begin{proof}
   209	  For real spatial Schwartz $f,g$, put $h(z) = \int f(y+z)g(y)\ud y$. Fourier
   210	  inversion and Parseval give
   211	  \[
   212	    h(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\widehat{f}(\xi)
   213	    \overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\ud\xi.
   214	  \]
   215	  Therefore,
   216	  \[
   217	    \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}h(z)\ud z
   218	    = (2\pi)^d\widehat{f}(-\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(-\xi)}.
   219	  \]
   220	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single test $h$ and reflect
   221	  $\xi$ using evenness of $\mu$. The spatial covariance is thus
   222	  $(2\pi)^d\int\widehat{f}(\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Summing
   223	  over the finitely many temporal factors gives
   224	  \eqref{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}. Schwartz decay, temperedness and temporal
   225	  integrability justify these pairings. If $W$ is initially given only on
   226	  compact spatial tests, smooth expanding cutoffs converge in the Schwartz
   227	  topology. The spectral form is continuous in that topology, admitting
   228	  $\mathcal{D}$ in the same completion.
   229	
   230	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}, applied with $H =
   231	  H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$, gives $\E W(\zeta_RF)^2 \le N_R(F)^2$. It annihilates
   232	  auxiliary-null tests. An auxiliary Cauchy sequence thus gives a Cauchy
   233	  sequence of noise evaluations in $L^2(\Omega)$, proving the contraction
   234	  extension and its uniqueness. Every finite linear combination of the limits is
   235	  an $L^2$ limit of centered Gaussian variables. Their variances converge, so
   236	  their characteristic functions prove that the limits remain jointly centered
   237	  Gaussian.
   238	
   239	  For the finite family let $A$ be the covariance matrix and $B$ the auxiliary
   240	  Gram matrix. Applying the norm inequality to $\sum_i b_iF_i$ gives
   241	  $b^{\mathsf{T}}Ab \le b^{\mathsf{T}}Bb$ for every real vector $b$.
   242	  Diagonalizing $B-A$ constructs a centered Gaussian vector $Z$ of that
   243	  covariance, independent of the evaluation vector $X$, on a product space. Then
   244	  $X+Z$ has covariance $B$. Conditional Jensen gives $\E\|X\|^p \le \E\|X+Z\|^p$
   245	  for every norm and $p \ge 1$. Finite Gaussian moments ensure finiteness of
   246	  both sides. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion}.
   247	\end{proof}
   248	
   249	The auxiliary completion depends on $R$ and $\zeta$. Its construction does not
   250	define multiplication by $\zeta_R$ on the original noise quotient. Nor does the
   251	finite linear Gaussian comparison assert a covariance comparison for nonlinear
   252	wave solutions. The auxiliary and original test norms need not dominate one
   253	another. No spatial representative for every auxiliary class, nonnegative
   254	physical inverse covariance for $\nu_R$, or uniform density bound in $R$ is
   255	asserted.
   256	
   257	\begin{proposition}[A physical mask need not preserve noise-null tests]
   258	  \label{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}
   259	  In the admissible case $d = 2$, $\alpha = 1$, $0 < a < 1$ and $\Gamma =
   260	  \delta_0(\ud x_1)\ud x_2$, there is a real compact smooth mask $\zeta$ such
   261	  that no finite $C$ satisfies $\E W(\zeta F)^2 \le C\E W(F)^2$ for every
   262	  compact smooth test $F$.
   263	\end{proposition}
   264	
   265	\begin{proof}
   266	  Fourier inversion on Schwartz tests gives $\mu =
   267	  (2\pi)^{-1}\ud\xi_1\delta_0(\ud\xi_2)$ in the stated spectral convention. The
   268	  measure $\Gamma$ is nonnegative, even, positive definite and tempered, with
   269	  $\Gamma(cA) = c\Gamma(A)$. It therefore satisfies Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}
   270	  with $\alpha = 1$. This is not spatial white noise in dimension two. For real
   271	  compact smooth $g$, its spatial covariance is, by ordinary Fubini,
   272	  \[
   273	    V(g) = \int_\R\left(\int_\R g(x_1,x_2)\ud x_2\right)^2\ud x_1.
   274	  \]
   275	  Choose real even $\chi \in C_c^\infty(\R)$ equal to one on $[-1,1]$ and zero
   276	  outside $[-2,2]$. For example, on $1 < r = |x| < 2$ use
   277	  \[
   278	    \chi(x) = \frac{e^{-1/(2-r)}}{e^{-1/(2-r)}+e^{-1/(r-1)}}.
   279	  \]
   280	  The endpoint exponentials vanish to every order, so the plateau pastes
   281	  smoothly. Let $I_\chi = \int(\chi')^2 > 0$ and $J_\chi = \int\chi^4 > 0$.
   282	  Positivity of $I_\chi$ follows because $\chi$ is not constant, and $J_\chi \ge
   283	  2$. Put $g(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi''(x_2)$ and $\zeta(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi(x_2)$.
   284	  Their unmasked marginal vanishes since $\int\chi'' = 0$, whereas integration
   285	  by parts gives the masked marginal $-I_\chi\chi(x_1)^2$. Thus, $V(g) = 0$ and
   286	  $V(\zeta g) = J_\chi I_\chi^2 > 0$. For a nonzero nonnegative $\tau \in
   287	  C_c^\infty(0,T)$, set $F(t,x) = \tau(t)g(x)$. The temporal factor
   288	  $\|\tau\|_a^2$ is finite and strictly positive because its nonnegative
   289	  integrand is positive on a set of positive two-dimensional measure.
   290	  Consequently, the full unmasked variance is zero and the masked variance is
   291	  positive. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}.
   292	\end{proof}

1	\section{Frequency estimates and both wave variance directions}
     2	\label{S:wave-variance}
     3	
     4	We now apply the covariance and temporal estimates of
     5	Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance} to the full wave phase. We retain
     6	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, write $a = \alpha_0$, and choose and fix
     7	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-gamma-range}
     8	  0 < \gamma < \min\left(\frac12,\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\right).
     9	\end{equation}
    10	The interval is nonempty because $\alpha+a < 2$. We use $\langle\xi\rangle =
    11	\sqrt{1+|\xi|^2}$ and set
    12	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-scale-profile}
    13	  B_\alpha(h) =
    14	  \begin{cases}
    15	    1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    16	    1+\log(1/h), & \alpha = 1,\\
    17	    h^{1-\alpha}, & \alpha > 1,
    18	  \end{cases}
    19	  \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    20	\end{equation}
    21	
    22	\subsection{A scalar row estimate for a measure}
    23	
    24	Let $\nu$ be a positive Radon measure satisfying
    25	\begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-translated-growth}
    26	  \nu(B(y,r)) \le C r^\alpha,
    27	  \qquad y \in \R^d,\quad r > 0,
    28	\end{equation}
    29	where $C \ge 0$. If the estimate is initially known for open balls, apply it at
    30	radius $r+\epsilon$ and let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ to obtain the closed-ball
    31	estimate. Neither evenness nor a density is assumed here.
    32	Using~\eqref{E:masked-frequency-pair}, define
    33	\begin{align}
    34	  \Phi_h(\xi,\eta)
    35	  &:= \frac{\mathcal{Q}_h(|\xi|,|\eta|)}
    36	  {\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle},
    37	  \label{E:frequency-row-kernel}\\
    38	  J_h(\xi)
    39	  &:= \langle\xi\rangle^{2\gamma}
    40	  \int_{\R^d}\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu(\ud\lambda).
    41	  \label{E:frequency-row-integral}
    42	\end{align}
    43	These are initially nonnegative extended integrals. In particular, the notation
    44	denotes a pushforward of $\nu$, not integration against an assumed spectral
    45	density.
    46	
    47	\begin{proposition}[Uniform scalar row]\label{P:frequency-row}
    48	  There is a finite $K = K(\alpha,a,\gamma)$, independent of $d,\nu,C,h$ and
    49	  $\xi$, such that
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-row-bound}
    51	    \sup_{\xi\in\R^d}J_h(\xi) \le K C B_\alpha(h),
    52	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{proposition}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  If $C = 0$, a countable covering by finite balls gives $\nu = 0$, and the
    58	  result is immediate. Suppose $C > 0$. For each $\xi$, let $\nu_\xi$ be the
    59	  pushforward under $\lambda \mapsto \eta = \xi-\lambda$. Then $\nu_\xi(B(0,R))
    60	  \le CR^\alpha$. For $q \ge 1$, put
    61	  \[
    62	    A_\xi(q) = \int_{|\eta|\le5q}\langle\eta\rangle^{-1}
    63	    \nu_\xi(\ud\eta).
    64	  \]
    65	  Choose $N = \lceil\log_2(5q)\rceil$, so $5q \le 2^N < 10q$. Splitting into the
    66	  unit ball and the annuli $2^j < |\eta| \le 2^{j+1}$ gives
    67	  \[
    68	    A_\xi(q) \le C\left(1+2^\alpha
    69	    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}2^{j(\alpha-1)}\right).
    70	  \]
    71	  The geometric sum is bounded when $\alpha < 1$, is $N$ when $\alpha = 1$, and
    72	  is at most $2^{N(\alpha-1)}/(2^{\alpha-1}-1)$ when $\alpha > 1$. Hence,
    73	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}
    74	    A_\xi(q) \le K_\alpha C
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    77	      1+\log q, & \alpha = 1,\\
    78	      q^{\alpha-1}, & \alpha > 1,
    79	    \end{cases}
    80	  \end{equation}
    81	  with a constant depending only on $\alpha$.
    82	
    83	  Set $q = \max(1,|\xi|)$ and $\epsilon = 1-2\gamma > 0$. On $|\lambda| \le 4q$
    84	  we have $|\eta| \le 5q$. Both bracket powers in $\mathcal{Q}_h$ are at most
    85	  one, since $a-1 < 0$. The contribution of this region to $J_h(\xi)$ is at most
    86	  \[
    87	    2\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q)
    88	    \le 2q^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q).
    89	  \]
    90	  If $\alpha < 1$, this is uniformly bounded
    91	  by~\eqref{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}. If $\alpha = 1$, the bound follows from
    92	  \[
    93	    e^{-\epsilon u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\epsilon},
    94	    \qquad u = \log q \ge 0,
    95	  \]
    96	  since $u e^{-\epsilon u}$ has maximum $1/(e\epsilon)$. If $\alpha > 1$, the
    97	  remaining power is $q^{\alpha+2\gamma-2}$, whose exponent is negative
    98	  by~\eqref{E:variance-gamma-range}. Thus, the near contribution is at most a
    99	  constant times $C$ in all three cases.
   100	
   101	  On the far region write $r = |\lambda| > 4q$. Then
   102	  \[
   103	    |\eta| \ge \frac{3r}4,\qquad
   104	    \big||\eta|-|\xi|\big| \ge \frac r2,\qquad
   105	    |\eta|+|\xi| \ge \frac r2.
   106	  \]
   107	  Each oscillatory bracket is at least $\langle hr\rangle/2$, whereas
   108	  $\langle\eta\rangle^{-1} \le 4/(3r)$ and $\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon} \le
   109	  1$. Consequently, the far contribution is at most
   110	  \[
   111	    \frac43\,2^{2-a}\int_{|\lambda|>4q}
   112	    |\lambda|^{-1}\langle h|\lambda|\rangle^{a-1}\nu(\ud\lambda).
   113	  \]
   114	  Enlarge the domain to $|\lambda| > 1$ and split it into dyadic annuli.
   115	  Applying~\eqref{E:frequency-translated-growth} to their masses bounds this
   116	  expression by a constant depending only on $\alpha,a$ times $C S(h)$, where
   117	  \[
   118	    S(h) = \sum_{j=0}^\infty
   119	    2^{j(\alpha-1)}\langle h2^j\rangle^{a-1}.
   120	  \]
   121	  Choose $L = \lfloor\log_2(1/h)\rfloor \ge 0$. For $j \le L$ the bracket power
   122	  is at most one. For $j \ge L+1$ it is at most $(h2^j)^{a-1}$. Since
   123	  $\alpha+a-2 < 0$, the tail is
   124	  \[
   125	    \frac{h^{a-1}2^{(L+1)(\alpha+a-2)}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}
   126	    \le \frac{h^{1-\alpha}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}.
   127	  \]
   128	  The inequality uses $2^{L+1} > 1/h$ and the negative exponent. The finite sum
   129	  is bounded by $1/(1-2^{\alpha-1})$ for $\alpha < 1$, by $1+\log_2(1/h)$ for
   130	  $\alpha = 1$, and by
   131	  \[
   132	    \frac{2^{\alpha-1}h^{1-\alpha}}{2^{\alpha-1}-1}
   133	  \]
   134	  for $\alpha > 1$. Since $h^{1-\alpha} \le 1$ in the first case, we obtain
   135	  $S(h) \le K_{\alpha,a}B_\alpha(h)$. Combining the near and far bounds, and
   136	  using $B_\alpha(h) \ge 1$, proves the assertion and finiteness of the original
   137	  integral. All constants arose from numerical shell estimates and are
   138	  independent of $d$. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}.
   139	\end{proof}
   140	
   141	\begin{corollary}[A time exponent above one half]\label{C:frequency-time}
   142	  For every
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-beta-range}
   144	    \frac12 < \beta < \min\left(1-\frac a2,
   145	    \frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right),
   146	  \end{equation}
   147	  there is a finite $K_\beta = K_\beta(\alpha,a,\gamma,\beta)$ such that
   148	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-time-bound}
   149	    h^{2-a}\sup_\xi J_h(\xi) \le K_\beta C h^{2\beta},
   150	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
   151	  \end{equation}
   152	\end{corollary}
   153	
   154	\begin{proof}
   155	  Both upper endpoints in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range} exceed one half, by $a <
   156	  1$ and $\alpha+a < 2$. If $\alpha < 1$, use $2-a > 2\beta$ in
   157	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}. If $\alpha > 1$, use $3-a-\alpha > 2\beta$.
   158	  For $\alpha = 1$, set $\delta = 2-a-2\beta > 0$ and $u = \log(1/h)$. Then
   159	  \[
   160	    h^\delta(1+\log(1/h))
   161	    = e^{-\delta u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\delta}.
   162	  \]
   163	  This absorbs the critical logarithm. No endpoint value of $\beta$ is used.
   164	  This proves Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time}.
   165	\end{proof}

   167	\subsection{Forms on the full phase}
   168	
   169	Choose and fix $T > 0$. Set $\Lambda = (1-\Delta)^{1/2}$, $s = 1/2$ and $E_r =
   170	H^r(\R^d)\times H^{r-1}(\R^d)$. On the complexification of $E = E_s$, use inner
   171	products linear in the first slot. The map
   172	\[
   173	  Jz(\xi) = \left(\langle\xi\rangle^{1/2}\widehat{z}_1(\xi),
   174	  \langle\xi\rangle^{-1/2}\widehat{z}_2(\xi)\right)
   175	\]
   176	is unitary onto $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$. The full massless wave group has
   177	Fourier matrix
   178	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-free-matrix}
   179	  S(t,\xi) =
   180	  \begin{pmatrix}
   181	    \cos(t|\xi|) & \sin(t|\xi|)/|\xi|\\
   182	    -|\xi|\sin(t|\xi|) & \cos(t|\xi|)
   183	  \end{pmatrix},
   184	\end{equation}
   185	where the sine quotient is $t$ at zero. Let $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$. Choose and fix
   186	a real even nonnegative $\zeta \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ equal to one on $B_1$ and
   187	zero off $B_2$, and put $\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$ for $R > 0$. For $I =
   188	[t_0,t_0+h] \subset [0,T]$, $0 < h \le 1$, and Schwartz phases $z,w$, put
   189	\begin{align}
   190	  v_z(t) &= [S(t)z]_1,
   191	  \label{E:variance-displacement}\\
   192	  G_w(t) &= -\frac{\sin(t|D|)}{|D|}\Lambda w_1
   193	  +\cos(t|D|)\Lambda^{-1}w_2,
   194	  \label{E:variance-dual-wave}\\
   195	  F_{z,w}(t,x) &= 1_I(t)v_z(t,x)\overline{G_w(t,x)},
   196	  \qquad \ell_R(I;z,w) = W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF_{z,w}),
   197	  \label{E:variance-actual-form}
   198	\end{align}
   199	where $W_{\mathbb{C}}(F) = W(\operatorname{Re}F)+iW(\operatorname{Im}F)$. There
   200	is no observation cutoff in this definition.
   201	
   202	We first assume $\Gamma \ne 0$. If $\Gamma = 0$, all forms and the column maps
   203	below are zero, so their bounds hold directly. For the nonzero case, let $\nu_R$
   204	be~\eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-measure} and set
   205	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}
   206	  L_\zeta = \|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1,\qquad
   207	  C_\nu = c_d^2L_\zeta^2C_\Gamma.
   208	\end{equation}
   209	Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm} gives a positive even tempered Radon
   210	measure with $\nu_R(B(y,r)) \le C_\nu r^\alpha$, uniformly in $R$.
   211	
   212	\begin{proposition}[Form and phase kernel]\label{P:actual-wave-form}
   213	  The tests $\zeta_RF_{z,w}$ in~\eqref{E:variance-actual-form} belong to the
   214	  original noise completion. The form $\ell_R$ is linear in $z$ and conjugate
   215	  linear in $w$, and uses the same $W$ as the model. For a smooth deterministic
   216	  coefficient $b$ with common compact spatial support and bounded spatial
   217	  derivatives on $[0,T]$,
   218	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-physical-adjoint}
   219	    \langle S(-t)B(b(t))S(t)z,w\rangle_E
   220	    = \int b(t,x)v_z(t,x)\overline{G_w(t,x)}\ud x.
   221	  \end{equation}
   222	  For a real compact smooth $\chi$, multiplication $D_\chi$ on both phase
   223	  entries has adjoint
   224	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}
   225	    D_\chi^{*,E}w
   226	    = \left(\Lambda^{-1}\chi\Lambda w_1,
   227	    \Lambda\chi\Lambda^{-1}w_2\right).
   228	  \end{equation}
   229	  With $U = Jz$, $V = Jw$, $r = |\xi|$, $\rho = |\eta|$ and the continuous
   230	  functions $c_r,b_r$ of Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}, set
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-kernel}
   232	    \mathcal{K}(t;\xi,\eta)
   233	    = \frac1{\sqrt{\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle}}
   234	    \begin{pmatrix}
   235	      -b_rc_\rho & -b_rb_\rho\\
   236	      c_rc_\rho & c_rb_\rho
   237	    \end{pmatrix}(t).
   238	  \end{equation}
   239	  Then
   240	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-covariance}
   241	    \E|\ell_R(I;z,w)|^2
   242	    \le \int\left\|\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2
   243	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   244	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta
   245	    \right\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).
   246	  \end{equation}

   249	\begin{proof}
   250	  The wave multipliers are smooth at zero through the continuous sine quotient,
   251	  with polynomially bounded frequency derivatives on finite time intervals.
   252	  Bessel multipliers preserve Schwartz space. Thus, $v_z,G_w$ and their product
   253	  are continuous in all Schwartz seminorms on $[0,T]$. For tests supported in a
   254	  fixed compact $K$, the absolute spatial pairing is bounded by
   255	  \[
   256	    |K|\Gamma(K-K)\|F(t)\|_\infty\|H(u)\|_\infty.
   257	  \]
   258	  Indeed, only $y \in K-K$ contributes to $\int\Gamma(\ud y)\int
   259	  F(t,x)\overline{H(u,x-y)}\ud x$. Combine this with the temporal Schur bound
   260	  and approximate the interval indicator and the continuous time dependence by
   261	  smooth interior temporal tests, keeping the spatial support of $\zeta_R$. This
   262	  admits the masked product in the original completion in every allowed
   263	  dimension.
   264	
   265	  We also identify its auxiliary and spectral limits. Approximate a
   266	  Schwartz-valued function on $I$ by time partitions with frozen spatial values,
   267	  and then replace the finitely many indicators by compact smooth temporal
   268	  functions. A diagonal sequence $F_n$ of finite temporal tensors converges in
   269	  $L^2$ time in every Schwartz seminorm. Fourier integration by parts and the
   270	  spatial weighted supremum bounds give, for sufficiently large fixed $N$,

271	  \[
   272	    \|\widehat{F_n-F}(\xi)\|_{L^2(0,T)}
   273	    \le \epsilon_n\langle\xi\rangle^{-N},\qquad \epsilon_n \to 0.
   274	  \]
   275	  Choose $N$ so that the square weight is integrable against both tempered
   276	  measures $\mu$ and $\nu_R$. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} gives
   277	  convergence in their spectral $H_a$ norms. Multiplication by the fixed
   278	  $\zeta_R$ preserves these $L^2$ Schwartz-seminorm limits, so the masked
   279	  differences converge in the $\mu$ spectral norm too. The preceding
   280	  compact-support estimate also gives convergence in the original completion.
   281	  Hence, the auxiliary extension and original-noise limit agree on these
   282	  products. Constants for this admission argument may depend on $R$; they are
   283	  not the uniform variance constants below.
   284	
   285	  For real tensor tests $f,g$, the Hermitian symmetry of their spatial
   286	  transforms gives
   287	  \[
   288	    A(-\xi) = \overline{A(\xi)},\qquad
   289	    A(\xi) = \langle\widehat{f}(\xi),\widehat{g}(\xi)\rangle_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}.
   290	  \]
   291	  Integration against either even $\mu$ or even $\nu_R$ cancels the imaginary
   292	  mixed term. Expanding the squared norm of $\widehat{f}+i\widehat{g}$, then
   293	  using the preceding approximation, extends
   294	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion} to the present complex tests:
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-complex-noise}
   296	    \E|W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF)|^2
   297	    = (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   298	    \le (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{F}(\lambda)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).
   299	  \end{equation}
   300	  This is a bound for the masked noise, not a declaration that its law is
   301	  stationary. Complex linearity of $W_{\mathbb{C}}$ and linearity of $v_z,G_w$
   302	  prove the stated sesquilinearity.
   303	
   304	  Smooth multiplication is bounded on each Sobolev space: Fourier convolution,
   305	  the inequality $\langle\xi\rangle^r\langle\eta\rangle^{-r} \le
   306	  2^{|r|/2}\langle\xi-\eta\rangle^{|r|}$ and weighted Schwartz decay reduce this
   307	  to the $L^1*L^2$ bound. The free matrix is strongly continuous and bounded on
   308	  $E$ on compact time intervals, directly by its weighted Fourier entries. Thus,
   309	  the ordinary first-response integral exists on states. Since $S(-t)(0,f) =
   310	  (-\sin(t|D|)f/|D|,\cos(t|D|)f)$, moving the real self-adjoint multipliers and
   311	  the two Sobolev weights onto $w$ proves \eqref{E:variance-physical-adjoint}.
   312	  The same weighted duality gives \eqref{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}. Inserting
   313	  this adjoint in $G_w$ is the correctly observed form; $D_\chi$ need not be
   314	  self-adjoint on $E$. This deterministic identity does not identify a
   315	  positive-width source with the original noise or assert a source limit.
   316	
   317	  The definitions give exactly
   318	  \begin{align*}
   319	    \widehat{v}_z(t,\eta)
   320	    &= \langle\eta\rangle^{-1/2}
   321	    [c_\rho(t)U_1(\eta)+b_\rho(t)U_2(\eta)],\\
   322	    \widehat{G}_w(t,\xi)
   323	    &= \langle\xi\rangle^{-1/2}
   324	    [-b_r(t)V_1(\xi)+c_r(t)V_2(\xi)].
   325	  \end{align*}
   326	  Their product gives~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel}. At zero frequencies
   327	  one uses the continuous sine quotient, not division by zero; at $\xi = \eta =
   328	  0$ the matrix is
   329	  $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-t&-t^2\\1&t\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Fourier
   330	  multiplication with the conjugate yields
   331	  \[
   332	    \widehat{F}_{z,w}(t,-\lambda)
   333	    = c_d1_I(t)\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2\mathcal{K}_{ij}(t;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   334	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta.
   335	  \]
   336	  The spatial integral is absolutely convergent uniformly on the finite time
   337	  interval by Schwartz decay. The Schur bound also makes it a Bochner
   338	  $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ integral. Reflect $\lambda$ using evenness of $\nu_R$
   339	  in~\eqref{E:variance-complex-noise}. Since $(2\pi)^dc_d^2 = 1$, this
   340	  proves~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} with no remaining Fourier
   341	  factor. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:actual-wave-form}.
   342	\end{proof}

   346	\begin{lemma}[Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality]\label{L:phase-bessel}
   347	  Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $\{u_k\}$ be a finite
   348	  orthonormal family in $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$, and let $g = (g_1,g_2) \in
   349	  L^2(\R^d;H^2)$. Then
   350	  \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-bessel}
   351	    \sum_k\left\|\int\sum_{j=1}^2u_{k,j}(\eta)g_j(\eta)\ud\eta\right\|_H^2
   352	    \le \int\sum_{j=1}^2\|g_j(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   353	  \end{equation}
   354	  The same bound holds with $\overline{u_{k,j}}$ in place of $u_{k,j}$.
   355	\end{lemma}
   356	
   357	\begin{proof}
   358	  Expand $g$ in a countable orthonormal basis of $H$. On each scalar coefficient
   359	  apply scalar Bessel to the orthonormal family $\{\overline{u_k}\}$, or to
   360	  $\{u_k\}$ for the conjugated version. Scalar finite Bessel follows by
   361	  subtracting an orthogonal finite projection and expanding its nonnegative
   362	  squared norm. Sum over the $H$ basis and use Parseval and nonnegative Tonelli.
   363	  The Bochner integrals exist by $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. A finite-dimensional $H$
   364	  uses its finite basis, and the zero space is immediate. No independence is
   365	  involved. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}.
   366	\end{proof}

   368	\begin{proposition}[Both variance directions]\label{P:wave-two-variances}
   369	  There is a finite $C_T$, depending on the fixed model, mask,
   370	  $a,\alpha,\gamma,T$, but not on $R,I$ or the orthonormal family, such that for
   371	  every finite complex $E$-orthonormal Schwartz family $\{e_k\}$ and every
   372	  Schwartz phase $z$,
   373	  \begin{align}
   374	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;e_k,z)|^2
   375	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2,
   376	    \label{E:wave-input-variance}\\
   377	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;z,e_k)|^2
   378	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   379	    \label{E:wave-output-variance}
   380	  \end{align}
   381	  For every $\beta$ in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range}, either right side may be
   382	  replaced by $C_{T,\beta}h^{2\beta}\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2$.

   384	
   385	\begin{proof}
   386	  Each entry in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel} is a product of two
   387	  continuous wave factors times $(\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle)^{-1/2}$,
   388	  with a possible minus sign. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave} therefore
   389	  gives
   390	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-kernel-time-bound}
   391	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   392	    \le A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\xi,\eta),
   393	    \qquad A_T = C_1(a)(1+T)^4.
   394	  \end{equation}
   395	  The positive even Radon measure $\nu_R$ satisfies the growth bound
   396	  \eqref{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}. Thus, all hypotheses of
   397	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row} hold, and
   398	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-row-bound}
   399	    \int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)
   400	    \le K C_\nu B_\alpha(h)\langle\xi\rangle^{-2\gamma}.
   401	  \end{equation}
   402	  No nonnegative physical inverse covariance of $\nu_R$ is needed.
   403	
   404	  The kernels used in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} belong to its stated $L^2$
   405	  space for each fixed $\lambda$. Indeed, $|c_r(t)| \le 1$ and $|b_r(t)| \le
   406	  \sqrt{2}\max(1,T)$ on $[0,T]$, by the high- and low-frequency representations.
   407	  The kernels are continuous into $L^2(0,T)$ in their frequency variables, hence
   408	  into $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ by Schur. Separability gives strong measurability.
   409	  Multiplication by shifted Schwartz components of $U$ or $V$ then gives the
   410	  required $L^2$ integrability. Later $\lambda$ integrals are of nonnegative
   411	  functions; their finiteness follows from the estimates below.
   412	
   413	  First fix $V = Jz$ and let $U_k = Je_k$ be the input family.
   414	  In~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} set
   415	  \[
   416	    g_j^\lambda(\eta) = \sum_{i=1}^2
   417	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   418	    \overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}.
   419	  \]
   420	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} and Cauchy--Schwarz over the two output components
   421	  give
   422	  \begin{align*}
   423	    \sum_j\|g_j^\lambda(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   424	    &\le 2\sum_{i,j}|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2
   425	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\\
   426	    &\le 4A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   427	    \sum_i|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2.
   428	  \end{align*}
   429	  Change variables $\xi = \eta+\lambda$ in the Lebesgue integral for each
   430	  $\lambda$, apply Tonelli and~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound}, and use
   431	  $\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}} = \|\langle\xi\rangle^{-\gamma}Jz\|_2$. This
   432	  proves~\eqref{E:wave-input-variance} with $C_T = 4A_TKC_\nu$.
   433	
   434	  Next fix $U = Jz$ and let $V_k = Je_k$ be the output family. After $\eta =
   435	  \xi-\lambda$ in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance}, put
   436	  \[
   437	    f_i^\lambda(\xi) = \sum_{j=1}^2
   438	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\xi-\lambda)U_j(\xi-\lambda).
   439	  \]

   441	  over the two input components bounds its right side by
   442	  \[
   443	    4A_T h^{2-a}\int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)
   444	    \sum_j|U_j(\xi-\lambda)|^2\ud\xi.
   445	  \]

   447	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$. Reflect $\lambda$ using the
   448	  evenness of $\nu_R$ and then use symmetry of $\Phi_h$. This row becomes

   450	  by~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound} with $\xi = \eta$. This proves
   451	  \eqref{E:wave-output-variance} with the same $C_T$.
   452	
   453	  Use Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time} for $h^{2-a}$ times the row integral at
   454	  the two applications above to obtain the asserted $h^{2\beta}$ bounds,

   456	  uniform in $R,I$ and family size. The $R$-dependent admission estimate was not
   457	  used as this uniform variance bound. This proves
   458	  Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}.
   459	\end{proof}

   183	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   184	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   185	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   186	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,

   190	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}

   192	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   193	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   194	  convention
   195	  \[
   196	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   197	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.

   200	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   201	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   202	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   203	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   204	  \end{equation}

3278	## SpatialStaticControls (whole result)
  3279	
  3280	Formalizes `L:spatial-static-controls` (Smooth temporal controls) of the
  3281	section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
  3282	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `975feb3`): statement lines
  3283	40-54 (the definition of `lambda_z(c)^2`, lines 42-46; the display
  3284	`E:spatial-static-score`, lines 50-53), proof lines 56-96. The section's
  3285	standing assumptions (lines 4-10) are a nonzero covariance from `H:homog`
  3286	and `a = alpha0`; `U_z = Gamma * z` pointwise for smooth compact `z` (lines
  3287	37-38). The wrappers carry `HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and
  3288	`Gamma != 0`, and use the exponent `alpha0`.
  3289	
  3290	Objects. `lamSq U c` is `sSup` of the real Rayleigh set
  3291	(`WeakSobolev.rayleighSet`) of the potential `c U`, that is the supremum of
  3292	`c int U g^2 - ||grad g||_2^2` over unit `g` in `H^1(R^d;R)` (weak
  3293	gradients); `lam U c = sqrt (lamSq U c)` and `lamZ Gamma z = lam (Gamma * z)`
  3294	is `lambda_z`. The definition is the TeX's display with a general potential;
  3295	for the bounded potentials used here the side condition of
  3296	`WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic (`isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded`),
  3297	so the set is the manuscript's set. `I_Psi` and `v_Psi` are the package's
  3298	`VariationalDilation.integratedRate` (the integral of the real-Rayleigh rate)
  3299	and `VariationalDilation.rawCost` (the integral form of the cost); their
  3300	identification with `sqrt(-E_s)` and `E W(Psi)^2` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`,
  3301	`L:compact-raw-profile`) stays outside Lean, as for `VariationalDilation`.
  3302	`B_Gamma(z,z)` is `OccupationKernelRow.pairing` (the extended nonnegative
  3303	integral of `E:spatial-physical-pair`) at `zE z = ofReal o z`;
  3304	`pairing_bridge` proves it finite and equal to `ofReal (int z U_z)`, and the
  3305	statements use its `toReal` only after that. `M_a` is
  3306	`TemporalEquilibrium.mass` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-mass`) and `f_a` is
  3307	`TemporalEquilibrium.density`.
  3308	
  3309	Part (i). `spatial_static_controls_rate_paper` proves, for a nonnegative
  3310	nonzero test function `z`: every `y -> z(x-y)` is `Gamma`-integrable; for
  3311	`c > 0` the Rayleigh set of `c U_z` is nonempty and bounded above (so
  3312	`lambda_z(c)^2` is a finite supremum), `0 < lambda_z(c)^2`, `0 < lambda_z(c)`;
  3313	and `lambda_z` is Lipschitz on every `[c_1, c_2]` with `c_1 > 0`. The general
  3314	form `static_rate` also gives `|lambda_z(c)^2 - lambda_z(c')^2| <= M |c - c'|`
  3315	for every upper bound `M` of `U_z` (the TeX's constant `||U_z||_inf`, lines
  3316	62-63) without any floor. Positivity rests on the named input
  3317	`RayleighFloor Gamma`: for every nonnegative nonzero test function `z`, the
  3318	Rayleigh set of `U_z` contains a positive value. It stands for the dilation
  3319	floor lemma of wave item L6-d at `V = Gamma * z`
  3320	(`VariationalFloor.rayleighSet_floor`); it is discharged under the section's
  3321	hypotheses in `SpatialOccupationCompleted` (`rayleighFloor_of_homog`, with the
  3322	completed wrapper `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper`). Disclosure: since `U_z` is bounded (proved here), this input
  3323	is equivalent to `lambda_z(1)^2 > 0` for every such `z`, that is to the
  3324	positivity claim of part (i) itself; the Lean content of part (i) beyond the
  3325	input is the finiteness, the transfer of positivity to every `c > 0` (through
  3326	`Gamma * (c z) = c U_z`) and the Lipschitz bounds. The TeX's positivity route
  3327	is different: a positive rate of a smooth test with mean `c U_z` through
  3328	`P:variational-unmasked-rate` and `P:compact-original-common-trial` (lines
  3329	57-62). The input is satisfiable (`rayleighFloor_volume`: `Gamma` =
  3330	Lebesgue measure, an unrestricted constant covariance outside `H:homog`:
  3331	it scales like `c^d`, i.e. `alpha = 0`, and it is not spatial white noise,
  3332	which is `Gamma = delta_0`) and fails for `Gamma = 0` (refutation
  3333	`FloorZeroCovariance`). The boundedness of `U_z` comes from the Gaussian
  3334	envelope (`VariationalMean.conv_le`), not from `P:variational-unmasked-rate`
  3335	as in the TeX (lines 60-61).
  3336	
  3337	Part (ii). `spatial_static_score_paper` states `E:spatial-static-score` in
  3338	the existential form (the owner's decision 2 of wave L6): `B_Gamma(z,z)` is
  3339	finite, the Rayleigh set defining `lambda_z(1)` is nonempty and bounded
  3340	above, and every `y < lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z)` is exceeded by
  3341	`I_Psi - v_Psi/2` for some `Psi` in `C_pos` whose rate and time cost
  3342	integrand are integrable on `(0,1)`. This is equivalent to the TeX display
  3343	whenever `S_1^pos` is a finite supremum; `spatial_static_score_sSup_paper`
  3344	gives the display itself, `lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z) <= S_1^pos`, on
  3345	the named input `VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma` (boundedness above of
  3346	`VariationalRate.score1Set`, that is of
  3347	`{I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}`, word for word the boundedness claim of
  3348	`P:variational-positive-scores`, `integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines
  3349	272-274, whose manuscript proof, lines 309-325, uses `T:full-upper`). Part
  3350	(ii) uses neither the floor nor `Gamma != 0`. The proof follows the TeX:
  3351	`Psi_n = f_n (x) z` (`ctrl`, in `C_pos` by `ctrl_mem`), mean
  3352	`k_n(s) U_z` (`mean_ctrl`), rate `lambda_z(k_n(s))` (`rate_ctrl`), cost
  3353	`(int_0^1 f_n k_n) int z U_z` (`rawCost_ctrl`), `k_n -> 1` with
  3354	`0 <= k_n <= 1` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-potential` via
  3355	`TemporalEquilibrium.potential_eq_one`), `int f_n k_n -> M_a`, and the
  3356	limit of the scores (`score_tendsto`); `ctrl_genuine` shows that every
  3357	Rayleigh set of `Psi_n` is nonempty and bounded and every integrand is
  3358	integrable, so no score is a junk value.
  3359	
  3360	Two bridges connect this module to `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`:
  3361	`pairing_eq_spatialPair` proves that the extended pairing
  3362	`OccupationKernelRow.pairing` and the real iterated integral
  3363	`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair` agree (and are finite) for continuous,
  3364	nonnegative, compactly supported functions and locally finite `Gamma`, and
  3365	`isUnitH1_of_unitTest` shows that a real unit test of `SpatialFourierBound`
  3366	with its classical gradient is a unit `H^1` pair. The weak gradient of a test
  3367	function (`VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test`), the radius lemma
  3368	(`VariationalFloor.exists_radius_fn`) and the score set, `S1Bdd`, `S1pos`
  3369	(`VariationalRate`) are shared with other modules and documented there.
  3370	
  3371	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: local finiteness of `Gamma` (`Gamma_radon`,
  3372	for Tonelli in `B_Gamma`); integrability of every integrand; nonemptiness and
  3373	boundedness of every Rayleigh set whose supremum is used; finiteness of
  3374	`B_Gamma(z,z)` before `toReal`. Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0` in
  3375	both wrappers (part (i) relies on it only through `RayleighFloor`), and the
  3376	fields of `H:homog` other than `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral`,
  3377	`Gamma_radon`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`.
  3378	
  3379	Proof-route differences: (1) the cutoff is
  3380	`cut_n(t) = smoothTransition((n+4)t - 1) smoothTransition((n+4)(1-t) - 1)`
  3381	instead of `chi(1/(nt)) chi(1/(n(1-t)))` (lines 66-72); `fn = f_a cut_n`
  3382	has the properties the proof uses (smooth, vanishing near the endpoints,
  3383	nonzero, `0 <= f_n <= f_a`, `f_n -> f_a`); monotonicity in `n` is not proved
  3384	or used; (2) dominated convergence replaces the monotone convergence of
  3385	lines 75-77 and 87-88; (3) the TeX's floor `c_0 <= k_n(s)` (line 78) is not
  3386	needed, because `lambda_z^2` is globally Lipschitz and `lambda_z` therefore
  3387	continuous on `R` (`lam_continuous`); (4) the mean and cost of `f_n (x) z` are
  3388	unconditional identities of Bochner integrals. Not formalized: the positivity
  3389	of `B_Gamma(z,z)` (lines 88-91), which the stated bound does not need; the
  3390	identifications of `lambda`, `I_Psi`, `v_Psi` named above; the finiteness of
  3391	`S_1^pos` (the named input `S1Bdd`). Constant potentials
  3392	(`rayleighSet_const`, `lamSq_const`) support the satisfiability check and
  3393	the refutations (`refutations/spatial-static-controls/`: the floor fails for
  3394	`Gamma = 0`, the Lipschitz constant `M/2` is false, `lambda` is not
  3395	Lipschitz on `[0,1]`, positivity fails for `z = 0`).

     4	Copyright 2026 Le Chen. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
     5	
     6	A deterministic Fourier bound for the physical spatial pairing, from
     7	`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (revision 975feb3): the quantities
     8	`A_sp(g) = B_Γ(g², g²)` and `b(g) = ‖∇g‖₂²` of lines 35-38 (with
     9	`B_Γ` of `E:spatial-physical-pair`, lines 12-17) and the first claim of
    10	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (lines 98-102) that `R_0 = sup A_sp(g)/b(g)^{α/2}`
    11	is finite.  This module proves the bound
    12	
    13	  `A_sp(g) ≤ 2^{1+α} R_Γ(1) b(g)^{α/2}`  for every real unit `g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d)`,
    14	
    15	with `R_Γ(1) = ∫ μ(dξ)/(1+|ξ|²)` (`SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1`; main TeX
    16	lines 7641-7650 at 975feb3), under `H:homog` for every covariance it allows,
    17	including `Γ = 0` and singular ones (`spatial_fourier_bound_paper`).
    18	
    19	This is a DIFFERENT ROUTE to the manuscript's "`R_0` finite": the TeX derives
    20	it at `integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` lines 142-145 from the finiteness of
    21	`S_1^pos` (`S1Bdd`, whose manuscript proof uses `T:full-upper`); the bound here
    22	is deterministic and makes `R_0 < ∞` independent of `T:full-upper`.  The
    23	consequence for `R_0` itself is drawn in `SpatialSmoothRatio`.
    24	
    25	Proof route (no TeX counterpart; every lemma here is a Lean-route step):
    26	* `A_sp(g) = ∫ c_Q dΓ` with `Q = g²` and the autocorrelation
    27	  `c_Q(y) = ∫ Q(x) Q(x-y) dx`; `c_Q = Q ⋆ Q(-·)` is smooth with compact support,
    28	  hence a Schwartz function (`HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap`), so the spectral
    29	  convention `HomogHypothesis.IsSpectralMeasure` applies to it;
    30	* `∫ c_Q(x) e^{iξ·x} dx = |Q̂(ξ)|²` (hand Fubini on `ℝ^d × ℝ^d`,
    31	  `fourier_autocorr`), so `A_sp(g) = ∫ |Q̂|² dμ` (`integral_autocorr_eq_spectral`);
    32	* `|Q̂| ≤ ‖Q‖₁ = 1` and, by integration by parts with `𝕜 = ℂ`
    33	  (`integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable`),
    34	  `|ξ| |Q̂(ξ)| ≤ ‖∂_ξ(g²)‖₁/|ξ| ≤ 2√b` (with `2|g||∇g| ≤ √b g² + |∇g|²/√b`);
    35	  hence `|Q̂|² (4b + |ξ|²) ≤ 8b`, i.e. `|Q̂|² ≤ 8b/(4b+|ξ|²)`;
    36	* `∫ μ(dξ)/(4b+|ξ|²) = R_Γ(2√b) = (2√b)^{α-2} R_Γ(1)` by
    37	  `SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog`, with `μ` homogeneous by
    38	  `MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, and the integrability of
    39	  `(1+|ξ|²)^{-1}` from `SpectralHomog.integrable_inv_one_add_sq` (`α < 2`).
    40	
    41	Also proved: `b(g) > 0` for a real unit `g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d)` when `d ≥ 1`
    42	(`gradEnergy_pos`; TeX lines 112-114 state it for `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`).
    43	Lean route: `b = 0` forces `∇g ≡ 0`, so `g` is constant and, having compact
    44	support in the noncompact `ℝ^d`, zero; the TeX argues through the Fourier support
    45	of a function with zero weak gradient (different route, same conclusion).
    46	
    47	Definitions: `autocorr` (`c_Q`), `spatialPair` (`B_Γ(F,G)` as the iterated
    48	Bochner integral `∫ (∫ F(x) G(x-y) dx) Γ(dy)`; for the continuous compactly
    49	supported functions used here it is absolutely convergent; the `[0,∞]`-valued
    50	form `OccupationKernelRow.pairing` is not used, and the identification of the
    51	two is not proved here; for continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative
    52	functions and locally finite `Γ` it is `SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair`),
    53	`spatialEnergy` (`A_sp`),
    54	`gradEnergy` (`b`, through the operator norm of `fderiv`, which equals the
    55	Euclidean norm of the gradient), `fourierQ` (`Q̂(ξ) = ∫ Q(x) e^{iξ·x} dx`, the
    56	convention of `IsSpectralMeasure`), `IsUnitTest` (smooth, compact support,
    57	`∫ g² = 1`).
    58	
    59	Supplied inputs: none.  Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the integrability of
    60	`c_Q` against `Γ`, of `|Q̂|²` and of `(1+|ξ|²)^{-1}` against `μ` are part of

    88	variable {d : ℕ}
    89	
    90	/-! ### Definitions -/
    91	
    92	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the autocorrelation
    93	`c_Q(y) = ∫ Q(x) Q(x - y) dx` (the inner integral of `B_Γ(Q,Q)` in
    94	`E:spatial-physical-pair`).  This is the package's one autocorrelation
    95	(`VariationalFloor` F3 is stated for it). -/
    96	def autocorr (Q : Rd d → ℝ) (y : Rd d) : ℝ := ∫ x, Q x * Q (x - y)
    97	
    98	/-- The real form of the physical pairing `E:spatial-physical-pair`
    99	(`integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` lines 15-17):
   100	`B_Γ(F,G) = ∫ (∫ F(x) G(x - y) dx) Γ(dy)`, as an iterated Bochner integral.
   101	For the continuous compactly supported functions used here it is an absolutely
   102	convergent integral (see `integrable_autocorr` and `SpatialSmoothRatio`). -/
   103	def spatialPair (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (F G : Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   104	  ∫ y, (∫ x, F x * G (x - y)) ∂Γ
   105	
   106	/-- `A_sp(g) = B_Γ(g², g²)` (line 35). -/
   107	def spatialEnergy (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (g : Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   108	  spatialPair Γ (fun x => g x ^ 2) (fun x => g x ^ 2)
   109	
   110	/-- `b(g) = ‖∇g‖₂²` (line 35), for a differentiable `g`, through the operator
   111	norm of the Fréchet derivative (equal to the Euclidean norm of the gradient). -/
   112	def gradEnergy (g : Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ := ∫ x, ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ^ 2
   113	
   114	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the Fourier transform in the manuscript's
   115	convention (the one of `HomogHypothesis.IsSpectralMeasure`):
   116	`Q̂(ξ) = ∫ Q(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx`. -/

   118	  ∫ x, (Q x : ℂ) * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))

   128	theorem autocorr_eq_convolution (Q : Rd d → ℝ) :
   129	    autocorr Q = convolution Q (fun x => Q (-x)) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume := by
   130	  funext y
   131	  simp only [autocorr, convolution, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply, smul_eq_mul, neg_sub]
   132

   136	  rw [autocorr_eq_convolution]
   137	  have hl : LocallyIntegrable (fun x => Q (-x)) volume :=
   138	    (hQ.continuous.comp continuous_neg).locallyIntegrable
   139	  exact hc.contDiff_convolution_left (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) hQ hl

   145	  exact hc.convolution (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) (hc.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.neg _))

   478	    Integrable (autocorr (fun x => g x ^ 2)) Γ ∧
   479	      Integrable (fun ξ => ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
   480	      Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ ∧
   481	      spatialEnergy Γ g = ∫ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ ∧
   482	      0 ≤ spatialEnergy Γ g ∧
   483	      spatialEnergy Γ g ≤
   484	        2 ^ (1 + alpha) * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1 * gradEnergy g ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   485	  obtain ⟨hs, hc, hu⟩ := hg
   486	  have hQs : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun x => g x ^ 2) := hs.pow 2
   487	  have hQc : HasCompactSupport (fun x => g x ^ 2) :=
   488	    hc.comp_left (g := fun r : ℝ => r ^ 2) (by norm_num)
   489	  have i1 := integrable_autocorr hQs.continuous hQc Γ
   490	  have hR := SpectralHomog.integrable_inv_one_add_sq hI ha2
   491	  set b := gradEnergy g with hbdef
   492	  set q := 2 * Real.sqrt b with hqdef
   493	  have hq : 0 < q := by positivity
   494	  have hq2 : q ^ 2 = 4 * b := by rw [hqdef, mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hb.le]; norm_num
   495	  have hRq := SpectralHomog.resolvent_integrable hR q hq.ne'
   496	  have hpt : ∀ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 8 * b * (1 / (q ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   497	    intro ξ
   498	    have h := norm_fourierQ_sq_mul_le ⟨hs, hc, hu⟩ hb ξ
   499	    rw [hq2, mul_one_div, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
   500	    exact h
   501	  have hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ξ => ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2) μ :=
   502	    ((fourierQ_continuous (integrable_sq_and_grad hs hc).1).norm.pow 2).aestronglyMeasurable
   503	  have i2 : Integrable (fun ξ => ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2) μ :=
   504	    Integrable.mono' (hRq.const_mul (8 * b)) hmeas (Eventually.of_forall fun ξ => by
   505	      rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (by positivity)]; exact hpt ξ)
   506	  have heq : spatialEnergy Γ g = ∫ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
   507	    integral_autocorr_eq_spectral hsp hQs hQc
   508	  refine ⟨i1, i2, hR, heq, ?_, ?_⟩
   509	  · rw [heq]; exact integral_nonneg fun _ => by positivity
   510	  · rw [heq]
   511	    calc ∫ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ
   512	        ≤ ∫ ξ, 8 * b * (1 / (q ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) ∂μ :=
   513	          integral_mono i2 (hRq.const_mul _) hpt
   514	      _ = 8 * b * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ q := by
   515	          rw [integral_const_mul]; rfl
   516	      _ = 8 * b * (q ^ (alpha - 2) * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1) := by
   517	          rw [SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog hI q hq]
   518	      _ = 2 ^ (1 + alpha) * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1 * b ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   519	          rw [← mul_assoc, scalar_identity alpha b hb]; ring

   521	/-! ### Positivity of the gradient energy -/
   522	
   523	/-- `b(g) > 0` for a real unit `g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d)`, `d ≥ 1` (TeX lines 112-114).
   524	Lean route (differs from the TeX's Fourier-support argument, same conclusion):
   525	`b = 0` forces `∇g ≡ 0` by continuity, hence `g` constant, hence `g = 0` by
   526	compact support in the noncompact `ℝ^d`, contradicting `‖g‖₂ = 1`.  For `d = 0`
   527	the claim is false (`ℝ⁰` is a point), so `0 < d` is needed. -/
   528	theorem gradEnergy_pos (hd : 0 < d) {g : Rd d → ℝ} (hg : IsUnitTest g) :
   529	    0 < gradEnergy g := by
   530	  obtain ⟨hs, hc, hu⟩ := hg
   531	  obtain ⟨_, i2⟩ := integrable_sq_and_grad hs hc
   532	  have hD : Continuous (fderiv ℝ g) := hs.continuous_fderiv (by simp)
   533	  rcases (gradEnergy_nonneg g).eq_or_lt with h0 | h0
   534	  · exfalso
   535	    have hae := (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun x => by positivity) i2).1 h0.symm
   536	    have hall : (fun x => ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ^ 2) = fun _ => (0 : ℝ) :=
   537	      (Continuous.ae_eq_iff_eq volume (hD.norm.pow 2) continuous_const).1 hae
   538	    have hz : ∀ x, fderiv ℝ g x = 0 := by
   539	      intro x
   540	      have := congrFun hall x
   541	      simpa using this
   542	    have hconst := is_const_of_fderiv_eq_zero (hs.differentiable (by simp)) hz
   543	    have : Nonempty (Fin d) := ⟨⟨0, hd⟩⟩
   544	    obtain ⟨x0, hx0⟩ : ∃ x0, x0 ∉ tsupport g := by
   545	      by_contra h
   546	      push Not at h
   547	      exact (HasCompactSupport.isCompact hc).ne_univ (Set.eq_univ_of_forall h)
   548	    have hg0 : ∀ x, g x = 0 := fun x => (hconst x x0).trans
   549	      (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hx0)
   550	    simp [hg0] at hu
   551	  · exact h0
   552	
   553	/-- **The deterministic Fourier bound under `H:homog`**: for every covariance
   554	satisfying `H:homog` (`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`, including `Γ = 0` and
   555	singular covariances; no `Γ ≠ 0` is needed or assumed) and every real unit
   556	`g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d)`: `b(g) > 0`, the autocorrelation of `g²` is `Γ`-integrable,
   557	`|ĝ²|²` and `(1+|ξ|²)^{-1}` are `μ`-integrable,
   558	`A_sp(g) = ∫ |ĝ²|² dμ ≥ 0`, and `A_sp(g) ≤ 2^{1+α} R_Γ(1) b(g)^{α/2}`.
   559	Hence `R(g) = A_sp(g)/b(g)^{α/2} ≤ 2^{1+α} R_Γ(1)` (see
   560	`SpatialSmoothRatio.R0_pos_finite`).  This is a different route to the manuscript's
   561	"`R_0` finite" (`integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` lines 142-145 at 975feb3,
   562	derived there from the finiteness of `S_1^pos`); it makes `R_0 < ∞`
   563	independent of `T:full-upper`. -/
   564	theorem spatial_fourier_bound_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   565	    (hH : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) {g : Rd d → ℝ} (hg : IsUnitTest g) :
   566	    0 < gradEnergy g ∧
   567	      Integrable (autocorr (fun x => g x ^ 2)) Γ ∧
   568	      Integrable (fun ξ => ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
   569	      Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ ∧
   570	      spatialEnergy Γ g = ∫ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ ∧
   571	      0 ≤ spatialEnergy Γ g ∧
   572	      spatialEnergy Γ g ≤
   573	        2 ^ (1 + alpha) * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1 * gradEnergy g ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   574	  have hd : 0 < d := by rcases hH.dim with h | h | h <;> omega
   575	  have := hH.Γ_radon
   576	  have := hH.μ_radon
   577	  have ha2 : alpha < 2 := by linarith [hH.threshold, hH.alpha0_pos]
   578	  have hb := gradEnergy_pos hd hg
   579	  exact ⟨hb, spatial_fourier_bound hH.spectral
   580	    (MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog hH) ha2 hg hb⟩
   581	
   582	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.SpatialFourierBound

   131	/-! ### Unit `H^1` pairs and the Rayleigh sets of `c U` -/
   132	
   133	/-- A unit `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)` pair: `f ∈ L²` with `‖f‖₂ = 1` and an `L²` weak
   134	gradient `g`.  These are the trials of `E:variational-real-rayleigh` without the
   135	potential side condition. -/
   136	def IsUnitH1 (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : Prop :=
   137	  MemLp f 2 volume ∧ MemLp g 2 volume ∧ HasWeakGradient f g ∧ ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1
   138	
   139	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  A test function with `∫ f² = 1` and its
   140	classical gradient form a unit `H^1` pair. -/
   141	theorem isUnitH1_of_test {f : Rd d → ℝ} (hf : IsTestFunction f) (hu : ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1) :
   142	    IsUnitH1 f (fun x => (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rd d)).symm (fderiv ℝ f x)) := by
   143	  refine ⟨hf.1.continuous.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport hf.2, ?_,
   144	    VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test hf, hu⟩
   145	  have hc : Continuous fun x => (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rd d)).symm (fderiv ℝ f x) :=
   146	    (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rd d)).symm.continuous.comp
   147	      (hf.1.continuous_fderiv (by simp))
   148	  refine hc.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport ?_
   149	  exact (hf.2.fderiv ℝ).comp_left (by simp)
   150	
   151	/-- The connection between the two unit-profile predicates of the package: a
   152	real unit test `g ∈ C_c^∞` (`SpatialFourierBound.IsUnitTest`, the profiles of
   153	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio`) with its classical gradient `VariationalFloor.grad g`
   154	is a unit `H^1` pair (`IsUnitH1`, the trials of the Rayleigh sets here). -/
   155	theorem isUnitH1_of_unitTest {g : Rd d → ℝ} (hg : SpatialFourierBound.IsUnitTest g) :
   156	    IsUnitH1 g (VariationalFloor.grad g) :=
   157	  isUnitH1_of_test ⟨hg.1, hg.2.1⟩ hg.2.2
   158	
   159	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Unit `H^1` pairs exist (a normalized
   160	smooth bump). -/
   161	theorem exists_isUnitH1 : ∃ f : Rd d → ℝ, ∃ g : Rd d → Rd d, IsUnitH1 f g := by
   162	  let b : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d) := ⟨1, 2, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩
   163	  have hb0 : (b : Rd d → ℝ) 0 = 1 :=
   164	    b.one_of_mem_closedBall (Metric.mem_closedBall_self (by norm_num))
   165	  set I : ℝ := ∫ x, (b : Rd d → ℝ) x ^ 2 with hIdef
   166	  have hI : 0 < I := by
   167	    refine Continuous.integral_pos_of_hasCompactSupport_nonneg_nonzero (x := 0)
   168	      (b.continuous.pow 2) (b.hasCompactSupport.comp_left (g := fun t : ℝ => t ^ 2) (by norm_num))
   169	      (fun x => sq_nonneg _) ?_
   170	    simp [hb0]
   171	  set c : ℝ := (Real.sqrt I)⁻¹ with hcdef
   172	  let f : Rd d → ℝ := fun x => c * (b : Rd d → ℝ) x
   173	  have hf : IsTestFunction f := ⟨contDiff_const.mul b.contDiff, b.hasCompactSupport.mul_left⟩
   174	  have hu : ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1 := by
   175	    have e : ∀ x, f x ^ 2 = c ^ 2 * (b : Rd d → ℝ) x ^ 2 := fun x => by simp only [f]; ring
   176	    simp_rw [e]
   177	    rw [integral_const_mul, ← hIdef, hcdef, inv_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hI.le, inv_mul_cancel₀ hI.ne']
   178	  exact ⟨f, _, isUnitH1_of_test hf hu⟩

   184	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  For a continuous bounded potential the side condition of
   185	`WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic: the trials are exactly the unit
   186	`H^1` pairs. -/
   187	theorem isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) :
   188	    IsRayleighTrial V f g ↔ IsUnitH1 f g := by
   189	  constructor
   190	  · intro h; exact ⟨h.memLp_f, h.memLp_g, h.weakGrad, h.unit⟩
   191	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩
   192	    exact ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, VariationalMean.integrable_pot_of_bounded hVc hVM h1⟩

   194	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.
   195	For a continuous bounded potential the real Rayleigh set is nonempty. -/
   196	theorem rayleighSet_nonempty_of_bounded : (rayleighSet V).Nonempty := by
   197	  obtain ⟨f, g, h⟩ := exists_isUnitH1 (d := d)
   198	  exact ⟨_, f, g, (isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded hVc hVM f g).2 h, rfl⟩
